name: BHBench-CR
description: BHBench-CR is an open-source C++/Rust benchmark suite for two-dimensional Barnes-Hut N-body solver variants. Five paired implementations provide a compact research and teaching codebase for comparing pointer-based and contiguous tree storage, recursive and iterative traversal, and parallel force evaluation using C++/OpenMP and Rust/Rayon under a common numerical model and interface. Version 1.2.0 adds manifest-driven builds and execution for external, multi-file implementations; separate force-kernel and state-update timings; configurable timesteps; conservation histories and state snapshots; sampled force output; and structural-memory diagnostics. Additional uniform-disk and clustered inputs complement the existing projected Plummer workloads. Regression tests cover numerical edge cases, timestep refinement and the external build/run interface. The accompanying experimental workflows include multiple input seeds and distributions, direct-summation baselines, worker-count scaling, independent double-precision force references, structural-memory measurements, short-time integration and conservation checks, and an OpenMP waiting-policy probe. An extended AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D campaign is complemented by two separately audited Intel Core i7-11370H laptop series of 430 processes each. The laptop series use identical solver binaries, runtime libraries, input files, stored references and case order, while recording distinct Windows power plans.
